market_context: United States/Canada; safe raw-chicken storage with USDA references and emphasis on cold-chain control, cross-contamination, thawing and early freezing.
title: How Long Does Raw Chicken Last in the Refrigerator?

seo.title: How Long Raw Chicken Lasts in the Refrigerator
seo.meta_description: Raw chicken should usually be cooked or frozen within 1–2 days when kept at 40 °F / 4.4 °C or below. Learn how to store it safely and when to discard it.
seo.search_intent: Know how long raw chicken can stay refrigerated and how to keep it safe until cooking or freezing.

excerpt: Raw chicken should generally be cooked or frozen within 1–2 days when refrigerated at 40 °F / 4.4 °C or below. Keep it sealed or inside a leak-catching container on the lowest shelf. If you will not cook it within that window, freeze it early.
content_html:
Raw chicken has a much shorter refrigerator window than cooked chicken. USDA recommends cooking or freezing it within 1–2 days when it is kept at 40 °F / 4.4 °C or below.

That short window exists because refrigeration slows bacterial growth but does not stop it. Raw poultry also adds a second concern: juices can contaminate nearby foods and surfaces if they leak.

Start counting when the chicken enters your home cold chain

If you buy chicken today and take it straight home, today is the practical start of your household storage window. Do not treat a package date as permission to ignore the 1–2 day rule once the chicken is in your refrigerator.

If you already know you will not cook it soon, freezing it right away is better than letting it sit for several days “just in case.”

Store it low, not above ready-to-eat food

Keep raw chicken on the bottom shelf or in another location where a leak cannot drip onto fruit, vegetables, leftovers or food that will not be cooked again.

If the original package may leak, place it inside a clean tray or container. That simple barrier greatly reduces the risk of cross-contamination.

Do not wash raw chicken

USDA and CDC advise against washing raw poultry because splashing can spread microorganisms onto the sink, counter, utensils and nearby food.

Cooking is the step that makes the chicken safe. Rinsing does not replace reaching a safe internal temperature and can spread contamination around the kitchen.

What about an unopened package?

A sealed package helps contain the chicken, but it does not make raw poultry stable for a week in the refrigerator.

Use the manufacturer’s date together with USDA guidance and any local requirements. If the package gives an earlier use-by instruction, follow the shorter period.

If the chicken was frozen and thawed in the refrigerator

Chicken thawed continuously in the refrigerator can generally remain refrigerated for another 1–2 days before cooking, according to USDA.

If you thawed it using cold water or a microwave, the strategy is different: cook it immediately after thawing.

Do not thaw chicken on the counter

The outside of the chicken can enter a temperature range that supports rapid bacterial growth while the center is still frozen. Safe thawing methods are the refrigerator, controlled cold-water thawing or microwave thawing followed by immediate cooking.

Leaving it at room temperature for hours is not simply a slower version of refrigerator thawing; it changes the risk.

Color alone cannot tell you whether it is safe

Raw chicken color can vary with packaging, oxygen exposure and other factors. A color change does not always mean spoilage, and normal-looking chicken is not necessarily safe after too much storage time.

Bad odor, sticky or slimy texture and a swollen package are reasons to discard, but the absence of those signs is not a reason to extend the recommended window.

Do not taste it or “cook it extra” to rescue uncertain storage

If you cannot remember whether the chicken has been refrigerated for two days or five, cooking it harder is not a reliable way to repair an unknown storage history.

With raw poultry, genuine uncertainty about time or temperature should be handled conservatively.

When to freeze raw chicken

If you will not cook it in 1–2 days, freeze it. The original packaging is often acceptable for a short period, but adding freezer-safe wrapping can protect quality during longer storage.

Divide large family packs into meal-size portions before freezing if that lets you thaw only what you need later.

Cooking temperature is a separate safety step

When you cook the chicken, USDA recommends an internal temperature of 165 °F / 74 °C. Measure in the appropriate thickest part of the meat without touching bone.

Safe storage and safe cooking are two different barriers. One does not fully compensate for failure of the other.

The short rule worth remembering

Raw chicken: refrigerator at 40 °F / 4.4 °C or below, lowest shelf, leak-catching container, and cook or freeze within 1–2 days.

If you already know you will not cook it in time, the best time to freeze it is before you start wondering whether it will still be okay tomorrow.

faq.question: Does raw chicken last one day or two days in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: USDA recommends cooking or freezing it within 1–2 days.

faq.question: Where should raw chicken be stored in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: On the lowest shelf, inside packaging or a container that can catch leaks and away from ready-to-eat food.

faq.question: Should I wash raw chicken?
faq.answer: No. USDA and CDC advise against washing it because splashes can spread microorganisms around the kitchen.

faq.question: How long does chicken last after thawing in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: Generally another 1–2 days before cooking, as long as it thawed continuously under refrigeration.
